description:
Parent: op-841p. The single hardest missing piece for an explicit-bed HTR-10 model, with the lines that prove each gap:

1. CYLINDRICAL BOUNDS MISSING. pack_spheres(radius, half_width, packing_fraction, seed) takes ONE cube half-width - crates/outram-mc-libs/src/pebble_beds/sphere_packing.rs:205 and :98-104. The HTR-10 bed is a 180 cm diameter cylinder above a conus.
2. TWO PEBBLE SPECIES MISSING. A single scalar radius, doc says 'all particles equal-radius' - sphere_packing.rs:99 and :195. The HTR-10 initial core IS the 57:43 fuel/dummy mixture; without two species there is no initial core.
3. PACKING FRACTION CEILING. MAX_PF_RSA = 0.38 at sphere_packing.rs:63, rejection at :211-216. HTR-10 needs 0.61. Plain RSA cannot reach it. PackingMethod::RsaDem and ::OdrDem both return Err(NotImplemented) at :160, proved by the test at :546.

So (3) requires implementing RSA-DEM or ODR-DEM. Reference: the Tan citations already recorded in crates/outram-mc-libs/src/pebble_beds/references.rs (TAN2026_RSA_DEM doi 10.1080/00295639.2025.2456456, TAN2026_ODR_DEM no DOI assigned).

Cross-check available: Choo and Xiao (2024, OPEN tier, crates/kovan-literature/open/papers/choo-htr10-criticality.json) generate their HTR-10 packing with LAMMPS discrete-element settling and report the radial distribution function peaking at 6 cm from direct pebble contact - a validatable signature for any packer that claims 0.61.

Also worth knowing: the measured 16890 balls and the 123.06 cm loading height are NOT independent - filling a plain cylinder to 123.06 cm at f = 0.61 gives 16890.0 balls (measured 2026-08-11 by htr10::neutronics::tests::measured_ball_count_follows_from_loading_height). A packer that realises a different fraction must reconcile with the ball COUNT, not the height.
title: HTR-10 rung 1 enabler: cylindrical bounds, two pebble species, and packing fraction 0.61 in sphere_packing

description: run_keff_csg over the nested reflective TRISO RectLattice gives k~0.90 where the infinite-medium k-inf is ~1.9 (confirmed by unbiased delta tracking on the same materials). Histories are lost in the nested-universe/lattice reflective crossing (the known stuck-history/MAX_EVENTS band-aid). This is the pre-existing issue that motivates delta tracking; surface tracking through doubly-het lattices is unreliable until fixed. Do NOT extend the MAX_EVENTS band-aid; find the root cause in geometry lattice/universe reflective crossing.
title: outram-mc: nested-lattice surface tracker under-counts histories in reflective TRISO lattice

description:
RESOLVED 2026-08-05. Both halves done.

DIAGNOSIS (corrected twice): the agents reported astest/catalo/bibfor/te as 'absent from the clone'. They were never absent from upstream — /opt/upstream/codeaster-src is a cone-mode sparse, shallow checkout and those paths were simply not in the include list. Our own clone config, therefore fixable.

FIXED: git sparse-checkout add catalo bibfor/te (15 MB), then git sparse-checkout add astest (582 MB; clone 88M -> 670M, 17G still free). astest now has 13,118 entries. Licence spot-checked GPL-3.0-or-later, in scope per section 8.2 as part of src.

KEY FINDING — THE ORACLE IS USABLE OFFLINE. code_aster does not have to be built or run. The .comm decks embed expected values, and the two kinds mean different things: VALE_CALC (3,960 of 4,268 decks) is code_aster's OWN computed value, so matching it is verification against code_aster; VALE_REFE (3,383 decks) is the analytical/experimental reference, which is the validation-grade comparison and remains a maintainer call.

THE comp0* FAMILY IS THE SWEET SPOT for a constitutive-law port: 87 decks driving TEST_COMPOR(SUPPORT='ELEMENT', RELATION=...), i.e. a single material point with full material blocks and no structure. They map directly onto a unit test of a ported law and need NONE of the FE machinery this crate lacks. Everything else in astest is a full structural run and does need it.

Coverage confirmed for every ported law: NORTON_HOFF 7 files, VENDOCHAB 8, ROUSS_VISC 5, VISC_GTN 5, META_LEMA_ANI 9, VISC_IRRA_LOG 5, GRAN_IRRA_LOG 9, IRRAD3M 13, VMIS_CIN2_CHAB 20, VISC_CIN1_CHAB 18, LEMAITRE 72, VMIS_ISOT_PUIS 5. Named entry points: comp008e (VENDOCHAB/VISC_ENDO_LEMA), comp010j (META_LEMA_ANI), ssnv230a/b (IRRAD3M).

docs/code-aster-port-scoping.md section 7 rewritten to match, including the corrected upstream path.

FOLLOW-ON WORK, NOT PART OF THIS BEAD: no ported law has actually been checked against astest yet. That is now unblocked rather than blocked, and wants its own bead per module. Still genuinely blocked and NOT by the sparse checkout: TFEL's hillTensor argument convention for the META_LEMA_ANI shear-slot question — TFEL is a separate project, absent from this clone entirely.

---
RE-FILED 2026-08-12 with its original id. This bead was created in an earlier session but never published, because beads-rs `bd` could not push the store ref (kopitiam#19). It survived only in the local v1 store, which diverged from origin's migrated v2 store. Preserved at ref refs/beads/local-preserve-20260812. Original status at preservation: closed.
title: code_aster scoping doc assumes astest, which is absent from the clone

description: Rod heatup plus Zircaloy-steam oxidation WITH the hydrogen source term and the reaction exotherm -- both currently absent. No relocation in this scope. Fix the broken 1800-1900 K window at crates/outram-park-fork-offbeat/src/corrosion/kinetics.rs:684-703, add Cathcart-Pawel proper and Baker-Just, and rename the CathcartPawel enum variant at kinetics.rs:306, which actually contains Leistikow and Prater-Courtright constants -- a reader trusting the name would MIS-CITE the model in a publication.
title: melcor-cor-lite: rod heatup, Zr oxidation with H2 source and exotherm
